name: Cryptic crossword No 24,561
preamble: Nine of the answers share a connection.

clue.text: Church split about art venue in capital city

blocks.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church
the ICA is the Institute of Contemporary Arts, a London gallery
to split is to leave, to go

explanation.surface: A congregation falls out over where to put its art gallery in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The ICA is the Institute of Contemporary Arts, a London gallery. 'Capital' here means first-rate rather than seat of government: CHICAGO is one of the nine musicals the preamble links.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is a great American metropolis; 'capital' is used in its sense of excellent, so a capital city is a splendid one.

clue.text: Man wants head of circus dwarf

indicators.note: the head of something is its top, so only the opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: first letter of circus
Happy is one of the seven dwarfs in Snow White

explanation.surface: A circus performer of small stature is needed by the ringmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dwarf' is not a small person here but one of Snow White's seven, which gives the cheerful one.
explanation.definitionFit: Chappy is an informal British word for a fellow or chap, a casual way of addressing any bloke.

clue.text: Be better off with Ecstasy for a short spontaneous performance

indicators.note: something taken off is removed, so a letter comes away

blocks.note: to be better is to get better, to improve
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone says taking a pill helps them do spontaneous comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better off' reads as one phrase meaning richer, but 'off' belongs with Ecstasy: the drug comes off the verb. 'Short' signals that the answer is a clipped word.
explanation.definitionFit: Improv is the shortened form of improvisation, unscripted theatre or comedy made up on the spot.

clue.text: Literally, an assistant to a dictator?

blocks.note: surface reading: a henchman serving a tyrant
setter's reading: someone who takes dictation, whose Latin name means 'by hand', is a secretary to one who dictates letters

explanation.walkthrough: A dictator here is just someone dictating letters. 'Literally' points to the Latin roots: the word comes from 'a manu', meaning 'by hand', so the clerk writes by hand what is dictated.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a literary secretary or scribe who writes down what an author speaks.

clue.text: Music makers, "Drifters", lacking a lead

indicators.note: without a lead means without the front, so the first letter is dropped

blocks.note: hoboes are wandering tramps who drift from place to place

explanation.surface: A band, the Drifters, has lost its lead singer.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'Drifters' look like the soul group, which fits 'music makers'; it is just wanderers. A hobo is an American word for a tramp.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument, so oboes are things that produce music.

clue.text: Transport both sides of a line in the desert?

indicators.note: things on both sides of something flank it, so they enclose it

blocks.note: two kinds of road transport, a car and a van
taken as written

explanation.surface: Vehicles parked either side of a track across the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' supplies two vehicles at once, one on each side of the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravan is a procession of travellers, traditionally camels and merchants, crossing the desert in single file.

clue.text: Cold, tail coat-curling Italian resort!

indicators.note: something curling twists and bends out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A chilly Italian seaside town where formal dress curls up at the hem.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'coat-curling' joins the anagram signal to its fodder; the tail coat is just eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattolica is a seaside town on the Adriatic coast of Italy, near Rimini, popular with holidaymakers.

clue.text: Director of half a car ferry, say

blocks.note: a car ferry is a ro-ro (roll-on roll-off) ship; half of that is one syllable
e.g. means 'for example', that is, 'say'

explanation.surface: The person in charge of half a ferry company.
explanation.walkthrough: A ro-ro is a roll-on roll-off ferry that cars drive straight onto. Nicolas Roeg was the British director of Don't Look Now.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicolas Roeg was a celebrated English film-maker, so he is an example of a film director.

clue.text: Instrument routine upended - vandal!

indicators.note: turned upside down in a down clue, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: a viol is an early bowed string instrument
a rota is a routine schedule of duties

explanation.surface: A hooligan has knocked over a musical instrument and wrecked the daily routine.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'upended' turns the schedule bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A vandal damages property, and one who breaks or defiles something can be called its violator.

clue.text: Rubbish Poles measure inside of hooter

indicators.note: to be inside something is to be held within it, so these pieces go in

blocks.note: hooter is British slang for a nose
N and S are the north and south poles
an en is a printer's unit of measure, half an em

explanation.surface: Silly talk about Polish people measuring the inside of a nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like Polish people but is the two compass poles. An en is a typesetting width; both pieces go into the middle of the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish in the sense of foolish talk is nonsense: both mean words with no sense or value.

clue.text: Letter of Swiss mountain hectares

blocks.note: an alp is a mountain in Switzerland
ha is the symbol for hectares

explanation.surface: A letter describing an Alpine estate of so many hectares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' suggests correspondence, but it is a letter of an alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Enjoying Nancy's delights? He won't, not being flexible

indicators.note: something flexible bends into a new shape; read cryptically, the letters are bent around

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rigid man refuses to enjoy the pleasures of a French town.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy is a city in north-east France, so its delights are those of a town; the question mark flags this playful definition. The phrase is also one of the nine musicals.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the town means going out to enjoy a city's nightlife and entertainments.

clue.text: Push blend of US pop and Lion King (short version)

indicators.note: a blend mixes ingredients together, so these letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
R, for Rex, is the short form of king

explanation.surface: A promoter pushes a mash-up of American pop with an edited Lion King.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lion King looks like one title, but it splits: the animal stays whole while the monarch is abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: Propulsion is the force that drives something forward, a push in the noun sense.

clue.text: The Mafia, short of a hit, casually turned over celebrity

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so letters are removed
done casually means done haphazardly, so the removed letters are scattered rather than together
something turned over faces the other way, so the remainder runs backwards

blocks.note: taken as written; that the answer also runs backwards inside these words is a coincidence of the deletion
these four letters are removed wherever they fall

explanation.surface: Mobsters who missed a target casually knocked over a famous person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit' sounds like a mob killing, but it is just letters to strike out of the phrase before it; what is left, read backwards, is the answer, another of the nine musicals.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrity as a state of being widely known is a synonym of renown.

clue.text: Medium reggae tempo, endlessly changing

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off
something changing takes on a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the word without its last letter

explanation.surface: A reggae song at a medium beat keeps shifting its speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' looks like a tempo marking for the music, but it is a painter's medium.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg tempera is a paint made by binding pigment with egg yolk, a medium used by artists.

clue.text: Do as you please, no matter what passes

blocks.note: first meaning: there are no rules, behave however you like
second meaning, read literally: whatever thing there is will be accepted

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the phrase word by word: any thing at all gets through. It is also a Cole Porter musical, one of the nine.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a situation without restrictions, where every kind of behaviour is permitted.

clue.text: Flower rather like a cat swallowing lithium

indicators.note: to swallow is to take inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: tigerly, an invented adjective meaning somewhat like a big cat
Li is the chemical symbol for lithium

explanation.surface: A flower that behaves like a cat that has eaten a battery.
explanation.walkthrough: The adjective is built by adding -LY to a big cat; the chemical symbol slips in before the suffix.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger lily is an orange lily with dark spots, a familiar garden bloom.

clue.text: As the art of making the base noble involves male in poisoned chalice

definitions.text: As the art of making the base noble
definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, 'like the art of...', matching the adjective

indicators.note: something poisoned is corrupted, so these letters are spoilt into a new order

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
taken as written

explanation.surface: The craft of turning base things noble involves a man trapped in a poisoned chalice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' and 'noble' are metals here, base metals like lead and noble ones like gold, which is what the alchemists sought to transmute.
explanation.definitionFit: Alchemy was the medieval pursuit of transmuting lead into gold; alchemic describes anything relating to that pursuit.

clue.text: American battle against alien American

blocks.note: anti means against
E.T. is the alien of Spielberg's film
Am. is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: An American fighting against a foreigner who is also American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American' appears twice: the first belongs to the definition, the second is an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Antietam, in Maryland, was the 1862 Civil War clash, the bloodiest single day of fighting in US history.

clue.text: Group from ship celebrating at the top of the stairs?

definitions.text: celebrating at the top of the stairs?

blocks.note: first meaning: sailors sent ashore from a vessel

blocks.clueFragment: celebrating at the top of the stairs?
blocks.note: second meaning, whimsical: a celebration held on the platform at the head of a staircase

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second, invented sense: the flat area at the top of a staircase is also called by this word.
explanation.definitionFit: Crews put ashore from a vessel are a recognised naval term, while the joke version is a festivity on the upstairs platform.

clue.text: Britain in poetry book held by an international player

indicators.note: something held is gripped from both sides, so it sits inside the other piece

blocks.note: a Lion is a player picked for the British and Irish Lions rugby team
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A poetry book about Britain carried by a footballer on international duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poetry book' looks like one item, but 'in poetry' belongs to the definition. The British and Irish Lions are a rugby side picked from the four home nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Albion is an ancient and literary name for Britain, used by poets such as Blake.

clue.text: Oil monarch's reduced comfort

blocks.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is the monarch's title cut to initials
ease is comfort

explanation.surface: A king's comfort is cut back by an oil shortage.
explanation.walkthrough: GR stands for George Rex, King George, as seen on postboxes. The answer is also one of the nine musicals.
explanation.definitionFit: To oil a machine is to lubricate it, and grease is used as a verb for the same action.

clue.text: Rocker possibly not opening locks

indicators.note: without its opening means without its first letter

blocks.note: a rocking chair is one example of a rocker

explanation.surface: A rock star who refuses to open the locks on a door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocker' suggests a musician and 'locks' a door, but the rocker is furniture and the locks grow on your head. Another of the nine musicals.
explanation.definitionFit: Locks are tresses growing on a person's head, a poetic word for what the answer names.

clue.text: Rice cooked with orange captivating Latin author

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are worked into a new order
to captivate is literally to take captive, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
amber is an orange-yellow colour
L is the abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: A recipe for rice with orange that enchants a Latin writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin author' looks like the definition, but Latin is an abbreviation and only 'author' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Ambler was an English writer of spy thrillers such as The Mask of Dimitrios.

clue.text: Game aristocrats lacking rights

indicators.note: to lack something is to be without it, so those letters go

blocks.note: duchesses are noblewomen
one's dues are what one is entitled to, one's rights

explanation.surface: A game played by nobles who have lost their privileges.
explanation.walkthrough: The removed letters are split: two come off the front and two off the end. Also one of the nine musicals.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is the board game of kings, queens and pawns played by two opponents.

clue.text: Tender spoken old king

indicators.note: spoken means said out loud, so it is the sound that counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: to tender is to make an offer

explanation.surface: A gentle old king who speaks softly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like an adjective meaning gentle, but it is the noun for a formal bid. Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia, builder of Offa's Dyke.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa ruled the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of Mercia in the 700s, so he is an ancient English monarch.

clue.text: Forecasters encountered at the rink side?

blocks.note: met is the past tense of meet, encountered
standing at the side of a rink, you are off the ice

explanation.surface: Weather forecasters bumped into beside a skating rink.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met Office is Britain's national weather service. The question mark flags the punning 'off ice'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Met Office is the UK's meteorological service, the body that issues the national weather predictions.

clue.text: A name one's rejected with an appreciative word

indicators.note: what comes with something is carried along inside it, so the answer lies within the following letters
something rejected is sent back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the last five letters of the first word

explanation.surface: Someone turns down a name offered along with a word of praise.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits backwards at the end of 'appreciative'. It is a name, Eva Perón's nickname, and the title of one of the nine musicals.
explanation.definitionFit: Evita is a Spanish diminutive of Eva, famous as the nickname of Argentina's Eva Perón, so it is a given name.

clue.text: Overturned political leader, one guarded by reticent body of troops

indicators.note: something overturned is flipped, so its letters run the other way
something guarded is surrounded by its protector, so it goes inside

blocks.note: PM is the Prime Minister
an means one
coy means reticent or shy

explanation.surface: A toppled leader is protected by a silent military unit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Prime Minister turned round gives the letters for a Member of Parliament. The answer is also Sondheim's musical, one of the nine.
explanation.definitionFit: A company is a military unit of soldiers under a captain, smaller than a battalion.

clue.text: "It's your joint," said (drunkenly) Native American

indicators.note: said means voiced out loud, and slurred speech blurs the sounds

blocks.note: the knee is a joint; a slurred 'it's your knee' comes out as two syllables

explanation.surface: A drunk offers someone a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like a spliff, but it is a body part. Say 'it's your knee' with a drunken slur, dropping the first syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shawnee are an Algonquian-speaking people originally of the Ohio Valley, one of the Native American nations.
